questions.title: Mitochondria contain their own DNA
questions.subject: fnd
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Genetics > Molecular Genetics > Mitochondrial DNA
questions.question: Which of the following cellular organelles contains its own DNA?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The rough endoplasmic reticulum is part of the endomembrane system and has no genome of its own; its ribosome-studded membrane synthesizes proteins encoded by nuclear, not organellar, DNA.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The smooth endoplasmic reticulum likewise carries no DNA; it is continuous with the endomembrane system and depends entirely on nuclear-encoded proteins.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The Golgi complex is a processing and sorting organelle of the endomembrane system and, like the ER, has no genome of its own.
explanations.D: Correct. Mitochondria possess their own small, circular, double-stranded DNA genome, distinct from and inherited separately (maternally) from nuclear DNA, encoding a subset of the proteins and RNAs needed for oxidative phosphorylation — strong evidence for their endosymbiotic bacterial origin. This independent genome is one of the strongest lines of evidence for the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria from free-living bacteria.

questions.learning_objective: State that mitochondria are the cytoplasmic organelle with their own DNA genome, and that this genome is maternally inherited and distinct from nuclear DNA.
